chapter: Ben Webster and Jim and Andy's
title: Ben Webster's friendship and the $200 loan
summary: He looked like a prophet, spoke eloquently on friendship, and later repaid a loan.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: And we remained friends. You know, we'd go out and play together. And he went with Duke Ellington's band and I wouldn't see him so often. And I got married and he got married, and we became -- our wives became friends. My wife was fascinated by him, well, so was everyone. He looked like a prophet out of the Bible, that's what he always made me think of. I always thought of the Lion of Judea. I don't Because when he talked--- know, that's what I think of./ He could have been a minister and converted the whole world, because he could talk with so much fire and enthusiasm.

And he was a great one on friendship. He had a great talk on friendship, it was the most important thing to him in the world. And I remember -- getting away from the story I'm telling, one night at Jim and Andy's, many years later, I cashed a check for two or three hundred dollars in the bar and I was sitting there, and I heard Ben say (inaudible), "Jim." I said, what? He said, lend me $200.00. I thought, oh, boy, but I'd heard what he said so I can't let him down. I said, here man. You see, that's what a friend is. And he was a good friend, he gave it back to me.
